slides.say: A player's score in a computer game is given by a formula. The score increases when the player collects more coins, C, and more stars, S, and decreases when the player makes more mistakes, M. C, S and M are all greater than one. Which of the following expressions cannot give the player's score?

There's nothing to calculate here. We check how each expression reacts when one letter grows. Each time, we change only that letter and keep the other two the same. [short pause] For each choice, we ask three things. When C grows, does the expression grow? When S grows, does it grow? And when M grows, does it get smaller? A choice that breaks even one of these cannot give the score.
at: For each choice, we ask three things

slides.say: [short pause] Let's solve it by understanding, one choice at a time. Choice number one, C plus S minus M. C and S are added, so when either one grows, the result grows. M is subtracted, so when M grows, the result gets smaller. Every rule fits, so this expression could give the score, and choice number one is out.
at: and choice number one is out

slides.say: Choice number two, C times S times M. All the letters are positive, so a bigger C or a bigger S makes the product bigger. That part is fine. But M is multiplied too, so more mistakes make the product bigger. That's the opposite of the rule. This expression cannot give the score, and choice number two is our answer.
at: and choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] In the exam you'd mark it and move on. But choice number three teaches something useful about fractions, so let's look at it. C to the power of S, over M. In a fraction with positive parts, a bigger top gives a bigger result, and a bigger bottom gives a smaller result.
at: C to the power of S, over M
In a fraction with positive parts

slides.say: When C grows, the top grows. When S grows, C is multiplied by itself more times, and because C is bigger than one, the top grows again. When M grows, the bottom grows, so the result gets smaller. So choice number three fits every rule. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: When C grows, the top grows
